title: Simple and multiple linear regression: coefficients and R²

videos.script: A correlation says that distance and delivery time move together. It does not say by how much. If a customer is six kilometres away, how long should Horta promise? {{promise}} Regression answers that. It draws the straight line through the points that misses them by the least, and the line becomes a formula: twenty-five minutes, plus two and a half minutes per kilometre. Six kilometres, about forty minutes. {{formula}} The slope is the useful part. It says what one more kilometre costs. {{slope}} Then the line can take more than one variable. Distance, the number of items, and whether it rained, all at once. Each gets its own number, and each number means: this much, with the others held fixed. That is how lesson eighteen's coupon shrank from ten minutes to less than one. {{multiple}} A model also says how much it leaves unexplained, through a number called R squared. And it can be pushed too far, in two ways. Asked about distances it has never seen. Or given so many variables that it memorises the data instead of learning from it. {{limits}} This lesson builds the line, reads it, and finds both edges. {{edges}}
